Yet it was not hidden from the Tayyaye (Muslims) that he was more inclined and leaned toward the side of the Christians.
And for about five months, in such vicissitudes as these, he conducted his kingdom.
And because the faithful, just, and righteous King Hetoum of Cilicia,
when he heard that Baydu had been victorious,
and that the kingdom of the Mongols had been established for him,
and that he loved the Christians,
and was inclined toward them more than toward the other religions,
desired to go in person into his service,
and to meet with him face to face,
and to confirm many matters between him and himself.
And when he went forth from his country,
he remained on the road for about two months.
And as he arrived near Siahkuh,
it happened that the great emir Nawruz arrived with the armies that were with him, in order to subdue Baydu.
Because the same Baydu was anxious within himself,
he then sent word through an envoy, saying to Hetoum, the Armenian king:
"Turn back, pray, to Maragha,
and rest there a little,
until I hurry and return to the camp,
and I will send and bring you to me."
And he did so.
And when he reached Maragha,
and stayed there about ten days, more or less,
Baydu fled before Nawruz, the great warrior,
and thus Ghazan, the King of Kings, arrived,
and went and encamped on the Black Hill which is near Dehkhwarqan.
Immediately King Hetoum made ready and went into his presence,
and offered him great presents.
And the King of Kings said to him:
"You indeed came to Baydu, and not to us."
Then the king replied:
"I am obligated to show submission to all the seed of Genghis Khan,
and whoever is established upon the throne,
I will come to do him homage."
Then the King of Kings received him graciously,
and clothed him in royal garments,
and commanded that a diploma (sigillion) be written for him.
[Hetoum] the Second,
the Armenian king,
accepted the faith of the Church of Rome.
And in the end he became a monk of Saint Francis,
and died in monasticism.
